newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua to slow devaluation of cordoba - Aleman.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua to slow devaluation of cordoba - Aleman.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman said on Wednesday that Nicaragua would slow the devaluation of its currency the cordoba against the U.S. dollar to eight percent a year from 12 percent.

This Central American government controls the exchange rate of its currency, devaluing the cordoba a fraction of a cent per day adding up to one percent of its value per month or 12 percent per year. A dollar was equal to 9.3636 cordobas on Wednesday.
"The slide of the currently definitely will come down from 12 to eight percent (annually)," President Arnoldo Aleman told reporters on Wednesday.
But the president did not say when the new policy would be instituted.
Aleman confirmed comments attributed to Central Bank President Noel Ramirez that were published earlier Wednesday in the daily newspaper La Prensa.
"Without wanting to create false expectations, a reduction in the slide, or devaluation, is possible," Ramirez told La Prensa.
He said the change was possible because inflation had been reduced to "practically zero."
The Central Bank reported April inflation at 0.32 percent.

The policy of gradually devaluing the cordoba under government control was started by former President Violeta Chamorro (1990-1997) as a measure to end the wild devaluations brought on by hyperinflation during the final years of the leftist Sandinista regime (1979-1990).
